title: A STEM-humanities faultline in IITs may have been exposed by Sahil death
content: Sahil Wakode’s death by suicide has sparked significant discussions about academic culture at IIT-B. The event has illustrated the divide between students in STEM and those in humanities. While some students view incidents through procedural lenses, others focus on social identities and power dynamics. The protests that followed reflected this differing perspective, highlighting underlying tensions on campus.

title: ‘Jaldi kar, Panvel nikalna hai’: Student’s joke leads to ugly spat with Nirma professor
content: During a comedy event at Nirma University, a student's remark led to a confrontation with a professor. The professor allegedly grabbed the student's collar and issued a threat in response. The National Students' Union of India demanded an apology from the professor and called for an impartial inquiry into the incident. The university has not yet publicly responded to these demands or commented on the incident.

title: Athens to Washington: What is the ‘Thucydides Trap’ Chinese President Xi keeps invoking
content: During discussions with US leaders, Chinese President Xi Jinping emphasized the concept of the Thucydides Trap, advocating for peaceful coexistence between the two nations. His repeated calls for mutual respect convey Beijing’s desire to evade conflict with the US. Historical instances suggest that shifts in power do not inevitably lead to war. However, analysts remain split over the implications of the Thucydides Trap in the current US-China dynamic.

title: Bihar: After Jamui, Samastipur, another girl harassed in public at tourist site
content: A video reportedly showing a minor girl being harassed in Banka has emerged online. Following this incident, police registered a case against six unidentified youths for their actions. The video appears to have been recorded six months ago at Mandar Parvat tourist site, according to initial investigations. Similar incidents in Samastipur and Muzaffarpur have previously led to multiple arrests.

title: Microsoft shakes up communications team; CEO Satya Nadella sends memo to employees
content: Microsoft is shifting its communications strategy to enhance the roles of its employees in public messaging. The company will move its communications team under Brad Smith's organization, focusing on legal and public affairs. Satya Nadella emphasized the importance of employees who are closer to products in telling Microsoft's story. Frank Shaw, the longtime communications chief, will transition to an advisory role as part of this restructuring.

title: Labourer’s son turns Rs 87,000 drone prototype into Rs 3.5 crore Army project
content: Sarvesh Sharma, an ambitious computer engineering student, has been awarded a remarkable Rs 3.5 crore grant aimed at innovating a radar-evading drone specifically designed for surveillance operations by the Indian Army in high-altitude terrains. This exciting development follows his recent achievement of fourth place in a national drone competition. With IIT Roorkee's backing, the project is slated for incubation and development over the next 20 months.

title: Meet Vishvavardhan Sharma, 9, who built an offline Gita app
content: Introducing Vrishvardhan Sharma, a gifted nine-year-old from Bengaluru whose early mastery of the Bhagavad Gita has brought him into the national spotlight. He completed many Gita parayanas and memorized Panini’s Ashtadhyayi, showcasing his dedication. Beyond academic pursuits, he ventured into programming, creating impactful apps such as GitaVardhan and KannadaVardhan to connect people with ancient wisdom. His unique ability to merge age-old scholarship with contemporary innovation has garnered him various honors.

title: Minnesota girl, 12, sent 100,000 bracelets to 50 countries, won $10,000 prize
content: At just 12 years old, Minnesota's Natalie Flaherty launched the 'I Stand With Anne' campaign, aimed at fighting hate in all its forms. She crafted more than 100,000 bracelets featuring her powerful message, spreading awareness across the globe. Through successful partnerships with organizations dedicated to Holocaust remembrance, Flaherty earned the prestigious 2026 Gloria Barron Prize. This passionate advocate plans to distribute more bracelets this Halloween, continuing her mission.

title: Meet Adrian Abraham, 9, aiming for world record with Grade 8 guitar exam
content: At just nine years old, Adrian Abraham is on a mission to pass a Grade 8 electric guitar exam in the UK, setting his sights on becoming the youngest achiever of this goal for a Guinness World Record. With a fervor for rock and metal music, he not only showcases his talents on stage but also creatively blends Indian music with Western rock on social media.

title: Intel cuts VP ranks from 450 to 200; CFO says ‘cultural problem’ delayed products
content: Intel has cut its vice president ranks from about 450 to 200 and halved management layers from 12 to six under CEO Lip-Bu Tan. CFO David Zinsner blamed a cultural problem of veto power and poor transparency for years of slow execution and delayed products. He said Intel 18A yields are ahead of schedule, 14A risk production is set for 2027, and gross margins have climbed into the low 40s.

title: Baba Ramdev explains why cheaper ghee does not always mean fake ghee
content: During a recent press conference, Baba Ramdev addressed questions about the authenticity of Patanjali's cow ghee. He emphasized that by utilizing various milk by-products, the company can offer competitive prices. According to Ramdev, India's significant contribution to global milk production ensures that no milk goes to waste post butter extraction, resulting in the creation of various dairy products that enhance their value and support Patanjali's pricing model for cow ghee.

title: Massachusetts turns retired cranberry bog into habitat for rare brook trout
content: Massachusetts is restoring Century Bog, a former cranberry farm in Plymouth and Wareham, to complete protection of Red Brook from White Island Pond to Buttermilk Bay. The restored wetland and stream channel could benefit about 60 conservation-priority species, including “salter” brook trout that move between freshwater and saltwater estuaries.

title: Man says working in ‘incognito mode’ helped him get promoted; shares tips
content: Harshit Mahawar claims that using incognito mode for office work has produced unexpected professional benefits. He believes it prevents employers from monitoring his browsing activity while working. Mahawar states he received better salary hikes and promotions as a result of this habit. He became the youngest employee to rise from a fresher to vice president in three years. However, there is no evidence that incognito mode directly influences career advancement.

title: 'Let's race, not wrestle': 5 takeaways as Trump-Xi navigate trade, Taiwan and AI
content: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met at the White House to discuss key issues like trade and artificial intelligence. They agreed to extend their trade truce by two months while significant disputes remain unresolved. Taiwan and its security implications were also central to the discussions, as Xi urged caution regarding the island. Both leaders emphasized the importance of avoiding confrontation and fostering cooperation between their countries.

title: IIT-Bombay student's iPhone remains locked, professor's statement not recorded
content: The Mumbai Crime Branch has recorded statements from 20 individuals related to Sahil Wakode's death. Investigators have struggled to access details from Wakode's mobile phone, which is locked. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is probing allegations of discrimination and harassment preceding his death. Wakode's family has demanded action against Professor Doolla while protesting at Azad Maidan. IIT Bombay has issued an apology regarding its earlier communications about the incident.

title: ‘Kashmiri Pandits driven out by Pakistan-backed terrorists’: India at UN
content: In response to Pakistan's statements at the UN Human Rights Council about Kashmir, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi asserted that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India. He denounced Pakistan's occupation of the territory while drawing attention to the systematic violence faced by religious minorities in Pakistan. Furthermore, Randhir Jaiswal dismissed Pakistan's assertions about the Indus Waters Treaty, reinforcing India's steadfast stance amid ongoing bilateral tensions.

title: ‘Lives may be sacrificed’: Saudi Grand Mufti urges troops to fight against Houthis
content: In a rallying call, Saudi Arabia's Grand Mufti has urged border troops to gear up for crucial sacrifices in the fight against the Houthi movement. He highlighted the necessity of reinstating Yemen's Saudi-backed administration amid escalating hostilities. Recent weeks have seen intensified assaults from both sides, with missile strikes increasingly threatening Saudi territory, as the Houthis target vital infrastructure and cities.

title: From Russia to India: Meet Yury Lisichko, the man fixing shooters' pistol grips
content: Russian pistol coach Yury Lisichko arrived in India in 2009 for a one-year assignment with the Indian Army. Years later, his Greater Noida workshop has become a stop for shooters seeking the right pistol grip. From Anish Bhanwala and Manu Bhaker to Jitu Rai and Sarabjot Singh, shooters have worked with Lisichko, who studies their hands, modifies fresh pieces of wood and keeps adjusting until the pistol and shooter work together.

title: Delhi’s old high-rises face mandatory structural safety audits under new DDA order
content: Delhi Development Authority has directed owners of older high-rise buildings to complete structural safety audits within three months. This directive applies to buildings sanctioned before March 21, 2001, with high footfall also included. Recent building collapses in Delhi have raised concerns about structural integrity and safety. The audit aims to assess the earthquake resistance of these buildings. Failure to comply may result in action against the owners.

title: PVR Inox ordered to pay Rs 6,000 after movie show cancelled 10 minutes after start
content: A consumer complaint was upheld by the Hyderabad district commission regarding a cancelled film show. The complainant experienced distress due to the abrupt cancellation of the movie after 10 minutes. The theatre management initially attributed the cancellation to low occupancy, and later to a technical issue. The commission found insufficient evidence supporting the theatre's claims for the show cancellation.

title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex opens over 100 points up, NSE Nifty50 trades above 23,000
content: Dalal Street began trading on a positive note after experiencing a significant decline earlier this week. BSE Sensex opened over 100 points higher, while NSE Nifty traded above 23,000. However, rising crude oil prices are impacting overall market sentiment and limiting gains. Foreign investors have also contributed to the decline by selling Indian shares worth over 50 billion rupees.

title: Vanderbilt's $5-an-acre sale in 1914 became Pisgah National Forest in 1916
content: In 1914, Edith Vanderbilt made a landmark decision by selling 86,700 acres of land to the federal government for conservation purposes, significantly below market value. This generous act was aimed at promoting her late husband's vision of preserving essential forests. The area ultimately became Pisgah National Forest in 1916, laying the groundwork for ecological protection and setting a visionary example for public land conservation in the eastern U.S.

title: Wyoming storage shed turns out to be 140-year-old Chinese laundry
content: A weathered Wyoming cabin used as a storage shed for decades turned out to be a 140-year-old Chinese laundry and bathhouse owned by Sam Sing. After an eight-year effort, the historic building has been moved to a museum, where it will be restored and used to tell the story of Lander’s early Chinese community.

title: "I complained and had to resign": Employee on cost of reporting harassment
content: In a powerful recount, Ritica detailed her decision to resign after encountering workplace harassment, met with inadequate responses from management. Despite reporting the incidents to HR, her cries for help were dismissed, leading to even more obstacles, including pressure toward her coworkers to file complaints against her. Ultimately, she felt compelled to leave, convinced that the situation would remain unchanged.

title: Rajinikanth’s ‘Baashha’ idea was born from a scene discussed during ‘Hum’ shoot
content: The iconic film 'Baashha', starring Rajinikanth, was born from a casual chat on the set of 'Hum' involving Amitabh Bachchan and Govinda. They brainstormed a police scene that never made it to the final cut. Inspired, Rajinikanth relayed this to director Suresh Krissna during 'Annamalai'. With their title in hand, they crafted 'Baashha', completing it in a mere five to six months.

title: Man's $899K bet on Nantucket cliff cottage: Still standing 5 years later
content: Massachusetts car dealer Charles Fotopoulos bought a 1951 Nantucket cottage for $899,000 in 2021, knowing coastal erosion posed a serious risk. He said he would be satisfied if the property lasted five years. Five years later, the home remains standing, but only a few feet separate it from a 40-foot drop to the beach below, as erosion continues.

title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu's Class 10 marksheet resurfaces: actress scored 887/1000 marks
content: Samantha Ruth Prabhu and her husband Raj Nidimoru are thrilled to welcome their first child soon. Alongside this joyous news, a nostalgic Class 10 report card showcasing her academic excellence has emerged online. With her pregnancy announcement, Samantha humorously reflected on her former scholastic achievements. As she embarks on the journey of motherhood, she seems poised to take a step back from her film endeavors.

title: Vedaant: Famous surname brings pressure, but I want my own identity in swimming
content: As the son of celebrated actor R. Madhavan, Vedaant Madhavan gears up for the 2026 Asian Games, aiming to carve out his niche in the swimming world. Prioritizing the 200m freestyle over his usual long-distance events, Vedaant is committed to training hard. Despite facing the pressures of his lineage, he remains intensely focused, embodying the spirit of discipline and perseverance on this competitive journey.

title: Kelce Beer Brand Valued: Garage Beer tops $200m after rapid growth; investors back expansion
content: Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s successful venture, Garage Beer, has received a new investment amid the star player's record breaking performance.

title: Iran gives US six days to meet conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz: Report
content: Iran has granted the United States a six-day window to address its conditions for re-establishing access to the Strait of Hormuz. Key points include the lifting of U.S. sanctions on Iranian ports and the release of frozen Iranian funds. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has engaged with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi amid rising tensions.

title: ‘It is unholy, it is illegal’: Iran President Pezeshkian denies nuclear bomb ambition
content: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reiterated the peaceful intent of the country's nuclear program, emphasizing that it is not designed for weapon development. He expressed Iran's willingness to cooperate with international inspections and reduce its stockpile of enriched uranium. Pezeshkian pointed to the US's preference for military action over diplomatic solutions as a key factor in escalating tensions, asserting that Iran's military stance is purely defensive.

title: Oil slips 1% as traders hope for US-Iran truce amid fresh attacks on Saudi pipeline
content: Following a tumultuous week influenced by geopolitical unrest and supply worries, oil prices have dipped slightly. WTI crude now stands at $93.52 a barrel, while Brent crude has retreated to $105.80. Ongoing negotiations aim to address the Middle East conflict, which has considerably strained energy supplies. In Saudi Arabia, military operations have further heightened supply concerns, underscoring the persistent instability in the region impacting global oil markets.

title: Keralam’s 24×7 specialty care rollout falters amid political pushback
content: The Health Department’s push to run 24×7 specialty care in general and district hospitals is faltering, with Punalur taluk hospital the only pilot site struggling to sustain round‑the‑clock services amid acute doctor shortages and local political pushback, despite promises of redeploying specialists and teleconsultations. Officials say the plan hinges on creating hundreds of new specialist posts, a request the Finance department has yet to approve.

title: What is analogue paneer, and why is FSSAI cracking down on it? | Explained
content: Analogue paneer is not necessarily an illegally adulterated product merely because it is an analogue. FSSAI has recognised “Analogue in Dairy Context” as a category. The regulatory concern arises when such a product is represented to consumers as conventional paneer or another dairy product

title: Changing culture of movie-watching
content: From iconic single screens to multiplexes, streaming platforms and movies watched at home, Hyderabad’s cinema culture has changed dramatically over the years. content: Rajendranagar ACP said the preliminary probe indicated that the suspects believed Waseem was providing information to police about their alleged drug-peddling activities.

title: Less Cost, More Choices: Decoding New Motor Insurance Plan For Vehicle Owners
content: IRDAI New Motor Insurance Rules 2026: It proposes capping remuneration for new-vehicle motor insurance at nil for third-party and 5% for own-damage.

title: ‘We’ve never gotten along better’: Trump, Xi strike warm tone at White House dinner
content: president Xi and his wife welcomed to the white house alongside first lady . both leaders spoke about the importance of ties between the two countries . a state dinner in the East Room brought together senior US officials, business leaders and executives .

title: SIR row: EC says Form 6, 8 with citizenship declaration were unanimously approved
content: EC officials said the declaration form was introduced for the ease of voters so that whoever gives it need not submit any other documents . special intensive revision orders related to Phase 1 in Bihar, Phase 2 in a dozen states/UTs and ongoing Phase 3 in 19 states/us had all listed Forms 6 and 8 with a mandatory declaration form on citizenship details of the elector or parents . title: Iran offers US 7-day plan to end war, reopen Strait of Hormuz
content: the Strait of Hormuz has emerged as a central bargaining point in efforts to end the conflict Iran has offered the united states a seven-day plan . under the proposal, Iran would reopen the strategic waterway and the US and Iran would restart comprehensive negotiations over Tehran’s nuclear programme . the proposal was similar to a memorandum of understanding reached by the two sides in June .

title: 'Looted Rs 94,000cr': CBI arrests Mahadev app key accused deported from UAE
content: abhishek Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI immediately after arriving from Dubai . he was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni - both continue to operate the gambling network .

title: Watch: UN delegates walk out as Netanyahu begins speech
content: the speech was marked by a walkout by dozens of delegates as he took the podium . he responded by calling those who left 'moral cowards' and continued his address to a hall . supporters cheered and applauded Netanyahu during parts of the speech .

title: Centre moves SC for 2-year window to implement OBC creamy layer verdict
content: govt says retrospective application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions . the ruling made the verdict implementable from 2012, when the case was first filed . court had in march held that the income of parents could not be the sole criteria .

title: 'Want China out of Tibet': Protesters rally in Washington amid Trump-Xi meet
content: the protestors are demanding that the Tibet issue be raised before the Chinese Govt . the meeting draws attention to several longstanding areas of disagreement between the two countries . president obama says he is confident the two nations can continue building a relationship focused on prosperity .

title: Watch: Rainfall triggers major landslide in Sikkim's Rimbi
content: landslide in Rimbi village under the Yuksom-Tashiding constituency of west Sikkim triggered landsslide . mud, rocks and debris slowed downhill amid continued rainfall . no loss of life has been reported so far in the incident .

title: Wangchuk fears 'encounter' after accusing govt of Ladakh atrocities
content: sonam Wangchuk said he feared he could be subjected to an 'encounter' for speaking out against what he called atrocities in ladakh . he said a year after police firing killed four protesters in leh .

title: Greg Norman bought Florida estate for $4.9m, sold it 30 years later for $55.1m
content: Greg Norman bought an 8.3-acre estate on Jupiter Island in 1991 . the property offered enough space for boats, guests and family life . they rebuilt several of its key structures and extensively renovated the rest . it was eventually sold for about $55.1 million in 2021, far above Norman’s original $4.9 million purchase price .

title: ‘Extreme tail risk’: Mark Carney says Canada considered risk of military attack by US
content: carney said his administration had examined the possibility of a military confrontation with the united states . he said it was an 'extreme tail risk' scenario that Ottawa had a responsibility to prepare for . his remarks come as relations between Canada and the us have come under considerable strain since president Donald Trump returned to office .

title: ‘Long skirts, good mothers': Italian minister sparks outrage over sexist remarks
content: italy's foreign minister apologises for remarks linking skirt length to marriage . he said women who wear longer skirts are more suitable for marriage and more likely to make good mothers . the 73-year-old deputy pm later apologised for the remarks .
